newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse volume at year's low due to unrest.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse volume at year's low due to unrest.

text.p: Volume on the Nairobi Stock Exchange slumped to a record low for this year on Monday because of clashes between police and opposition-backed protesters demanding constitutional reforms.
The index edged up 17.46 points but turnover was posted at the year's low of 5.1 billion shillings traded on 140,382 shares compared to 15.5 million shillings on 356,719 shares on Friday.
"It's very slow, very dull. Most firms did not report to the floor," said a bourse official, adding that most dealers abandoned the floor and went home before the official close of Monday's trading.

Police said three people were killed and a policeman was shot and wounded on Monday. Police broke up rallies in Nairobi and several towns where most businesses failed to open and the streets were deserted.
Kenya Airways closed at 8.10 from 8.25 while Uchumi Supermarket eased to 38 from 38.25.
Kenya Commercial Bank gained seven shillings to close at 108 while Barclays Bank edged up a shilling to close at 111.
Brokers said this was the second time in three weeks trading at the NSE had been interrupted by political unrest.
"Offshore investors have not been too alarmed because the riots have been confined to the city but when we get to the depths of countrywide, I think it is serious," a financial analyst said.
Kenya Breweries edged up to 57.50 from 57 while East African Portland Cement closed at 42.50 from 41.
